title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenues due to increased government demand for sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: SpaceNews correspondent Debra Werner hosts a panel of experts to discuss the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space. The discussion was recorded in May.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is launching its new STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference. This space-grade product line will be showcased in Salt Lake City, Utah.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to integrate an optical communications terminal on its SWIRSAT-1 mission, leveraging Transcelestial's Space Optical Network for enhanced data transmission.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Proteus Space has been selected by The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory for an advanced on-orbit mission. The collaboration aims to deliver rapid, end-to-end access to space.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. The company, a designer and manufacturer of precision motion and control systems, announced this development.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been selected to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a launch scheduled in 2027. The company, based in Rochester, NY, specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is the One Space Event You Cannot Miss
summary: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is highlighted as a must-attend event for the global space community. The IAC has been a pivotal annual gathering for over 75 years.

title: New 'Star Trek' documentary featuring William Shatner hits theaters this fall, celebrating 60 years of Trek
summary: A new documentary titled 'Star Trek' featuring William Shatner will premiere in theaters this fall, commemorating 60 years of the franchise. The film is described as a tribute to the iconic series.

title: How a huge fleet of 17 spacecraft discovered something surprising about solar eruptions
summary: A fleet of 17 spacecraft measured a solar eruption from multiple vantage points, revealing its true extent. This discovery highlights the importance of distributed space observations for understanding solar phenomena.

title: Bad weather delays launch of China's historic Chang'e 7 mission to moon's south pole
summary: Bad weather has delayed China's Chang'e 7 mission to the moon's south pole. The new launch date has not been announced.

title: Launching 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn? NASA funds 18 futuristic spaceflight ideas
summary: NASA has selected 18 futuristic spaceflight concepts, including a proposal to launch 10,000 tiny 'femtosats' to Saturn, for its Innovative Advanced Concepts awards. These awards aim to support cutting-edge research and turn unconventional ideas into viable technologies.

title: How will NASA's astronaut training hub change with commercial space stations?
summary: NASA's astronaut training hub at Johnson Space Center is evolving to incorporate commercial space stations as part of future human spaceflight collaborations with private industry.

title: 'We Want to Believe' book explores the reality of UFOs: 'It's always going to be more likely that someone is wrong about what they saw' (interview)
summary: The book 'We Want to Believe' by Adam Kirsch examines humanity's fascination with UFOs and suggests that misinterpretations are more likely than extraterrestrial encounters. The interview highlights Kirsch's perspective on the cultural and psychological aspects of UFO sightings.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 224 — The Science of Artemis
summary: The latest episode of This Week In Space discusses the science behind NASA's Artemis Program's lunar exploration plans with guest Dr. David Kring. The podcast explores the objectives, strategies, and scientific goals of the Artemis missions.

title: SpaceX sends 27 Starlink satellites to orbit on 100th Falcon rocket launch of the year (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites into orbit from California on August 22, marking the 100th mission of the year for its Falcon rocket family.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 22, 1963: X-15 sets world altitude record
summary: On August 22, 1963, U.S. Air Force Captain Joe Walker set a world altitude record by flying an X-15 rocket plane higher than any pilot had previously achieved.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4982–4987: Back to Our Regularly Scheduled Programming
summary: The Curiosity Mars rover resumed its standard operations after a brief detour to study an erosional surface. It is now back on track to continue its ascent of Mount Sharp.

title: APOD: 2026 August 22 – Mostly Perseids
summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 22, 2026, features an image related to the Perseids meteor shower. The post is part of NASA's APOD series, which highlights daily astronomy images with explanations by professional astronomers.

title: NASA Shares Views of August Solar Eclipse from Ground, Air, Space
summary: NASA captured views of the August solar eclipse from multiple vantage points, including ground, air, and space. The eclipse revealed the Sun's corona over Greenland, Iceland, and Spain.

title: TB 26-04 Updates and Modernization of NASA’s Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA) Code
summary: NASA has updated and modernized its Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA) code, a critical tool for propulsion system analysis. The CEA code is widely used for equilibrium chemistry, rocket performance, and shock/detonation calculations in the aerospace community.

title: Webb Opens Treasure Chest
summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope captured an infrared image of the Carina Nebula's 'Treasure Chest,' a cometary globule in a star-forming region. The feature, known as the Cosmic Cliffs, highlights dense gas and dust clouds.

title: NASA’s Artemis II Crew Set to Receive Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: NASA's Artemis II crew members will receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor from President Trump during a ceremony at Johnson Space Center. The award recognizes the astronauts' upcoming lunar mission.

title: Europe’s Scorching Summer
summary: Europe experienced unprecedented heat waves in 2026, shattering temperature records and causing significant environmental and societal impacts. The extreme weather events highlighted ongoing climate change challenges.

title: SmallSat 2026
summary: NASA will participate in SmallSat 2026 with storytelling sessions by experts and booths in the Exhibit Hall. The event will feature presentations on smallsats, technology, and missions.

title: Artemis Mission Patches
summary: NASA conducted a terminal countdown simulation for the Artemis III mission at Kennedy Space Center, featuring mission patches from Artemis I and II. The event took place inside the Rocco A. Petrone Launch Control Center.

title: NASA Selects University Teams to Help Advance Aviation Research
summary: NASA has selected four university teams to advance aviation research through projects like supersonic propulsion and noise reduction for urban flights. The initiative, part of the University Leadership Initiative, supports student contributions to real-world flight research aligned with NASA's aeronautics goals.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch date of August 30 after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones. The telescope is now in the final stages of preparation for its upcoming mission.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a milestone landing, marking a significant event for Chinese commercial rocketry.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine production for its Nova rocket, aiming for a potential debut in 2026. This development highlights progress in reusable launch vehicles beyond Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, completed its second flight with a successful first-stage landing. This achievement is a significant milestone for the company's reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure, while SpaceX's Starlink launches also feature prominently in the upcoming week's space activities.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block. The company is making progress on multiple fronts.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral by restoring its primary pad at LC-36A while also utilizing another pad. The company aims to expand its launch capabilities with this initiative.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves mark the company's expansion and innovation in the space industry.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return. The project aims to advance European reusable space transportation capabilities.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission is a collaboration led by the European Space Agency (ESA).

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3, a space mission, will observe a double eclipse where the Moon crosses its field of view. This event is part of the mission's scientific objectives.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing for the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to study the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to observe the corona for longer periods than a natural eclipse.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: ESA is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This offers a unique opportunity to test software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical centre in the Netherlands. The payload transitioned from drone flight to sounding rocket testing.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites, one serving as a coronagraph to block the Sun's glare and observe the solar corona. The mission aims to study the Sun's atmosphere in unprecedented detail.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: SpaceWERX announced the newest awardees of the 2026 STRATFI program during the Fed Supernova conference. The Space Force revealed the recipients of the Strategic Funding Increase program.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, discusses the key technologies shaping the future of space tech in an op-ed. The article highlights emerging innovations that could redefine the space industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its satellite production capacity and enhance mission capabilities. The investment will support broader mission types and increased manufacturing scale.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while collaborating with Maverick Space Systems to sell the remaining fairing space for rideshare opportunities in a constrained launch market.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to expand its mobile services to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon. The company aims to tap into a multi-billion-dollar revenue opportunity by moving beyond its current direct-to-consumer satellite coverage.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.
company: Office of Science and Technology Policy

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a radioisotope heating unit (RHU) to the Moon on a 2028 mission. The mission aims to demonstrate Zeno's technology for keeping a 5W payload operational in lunar conditions.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The Space Force's FY27 budget request reached a record $71.3 billion, making headlines earlier this year. The budget highlights significant investments in defense space capabilities.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in tracking and managing space assets more effectively.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, leads Germany's military space operations to protect assets and integrate space capabilities. The discussion highlights Germany's focus on space defense and military integration.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to bolster the U.S. space industry's capacity and competitiveness.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the shift to the 'space edge' rather than orbital data centers. It features insights from Voyager's CTO, Paul Tilghman.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Orbital data center startup Starcloud raised an additional $250 million for its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion just five months after the initial raise. The funding round was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway has appointed Rune Jensen as acting CEO following Morten Tengs' departure at the end of August. The company will now search for a permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics has secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal marks a significant expansion in Sypris Electronics' involvement in next-generation space technology.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its large-scale satellite constellation development and enhance mission capabilities. This investment marks a significant milestone in the company's growth trajectory.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its chief operating officer to oversee day-to-day operations, operational efficiency, capital formation, and business scaling. The move aims to support the company's growth as it ramps up operations.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS on August 21 from New Zealand. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth launch for the Japanese company.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium, marking a significant move in the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition.
